entries.title: Genesis 43:5
segments: As to the future doing of things which are left to our discretion, it is ordinarily not best to say positively what we will or will not do, but to feel our dependence on God; and when the time to act comes, decide as truth and duty may then require.

entries.title: Genesis 43:7
segments:
According to the tenor of these words; suited our answers honestly to these questions of his. 
 
When things seem to go against us, we are apt to overlook the controlling hand of God, and regard only the instruments; but in blaming them, we often find fault with him.

entries.title: Genesis 43:11
segments:
Balm; balsam, like that of Gilead. 
 
  Honey; probably here honey of grapes, made by boiling down new wine to a third or half. 
 
  Myrrh; here probably a fragrant gum called ladanum. 
 
  Nuts; the original word means pistacia-nuts. 
 
When a man has promised to do what is wrong, instead of feeling that he is bound to fulfil his promise, his duty is to acknowledge his sin in making it, repent, and do what is right.  There is always a law higher than any mere human promise, namely, the law of God.  If a man does wrong because he has promised or sworn to do it, he adds sin to sin, and ripens for an aggravated condemnation.

entries.title: Genesis 43:12
segments: Double money; that which they brought back, and enough more to buy the corn which they needed.

entries.title: Genesis 43:14
segments: If I be bereaved--I am bereaved; an expression of desponding resignation.

entries.title: Genesis 43:18
segments: A guilty conscience, when awakened, naturally forebodes evil, producing a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation; and unless men find the way of deliverance, it wil make them wretched.

entries.title: Genesis 43:22
segments: Property that has come into our hands by oversight or mistake, as well as that which we have wrongfully obtained, should be carefully and promptly returned to its rightful owners.

entries.title: Genesis 43:23
segments:
God--hath given you treasure; not without human agency; but he had so ordered things in his providence that they had their money. 
 
  I had your money; it was paid to me, and I acknowledge the receipt of it; of course you need not fear.  He had himself, at the command of Joseph, without their knowledge, put it into their sacks.

entries.title: Genesis 43:24
segments: Washed their feet; according to the custom of travellers in those days.

entries.title: Genesis 43:25
segments: The present; that which they had brought from the land of Canaan.

entries.title: Genesis 43:26
segments: When events, long before made known, are accomplished by the voluntary actions of free moral agents, it shows that such actions were beforehand certain; though that certainty does not lessen men's freedom, nor diminish their praise or blameworthiness in performing those actions.

entries.title: Genesis 43:30
segments: Family ties are tender and lasting; and delightful, after long absence, is the meeting of affectionate family friends.  As their forcible and violent separation causes the intensest anguish, so their kind, providential restoration gives inexpressible joy.

entries.title: Genesis 43:31
segments: Refrained; from weeping, and appeared as usual.

entries.title: Genesis 43:32
segments: For that is an abomination; the Egyptians kept themselves separate from all strangers, and had a particular aversion to men whose occupation was that of shepherds.

entries.title: Genesis 43:33
segments:
They sat before him; they were seated according to their different ages. 
 
  Marvelled; that he who seated them should know, in each case, which was oldest.
